entries.title: Opened: $1,000, trades only on Vamsi's direction
entries.body:
Start: $1,000 paper cash, Sat Oct 3. Default finish: the Mon Oct 5, 4:00 PM ET close, the same line as the other two books; Vamsi can extend it.
Instruments: stocks, ETFs (leveraged and inverse included), listed options (regular session; buy at the ask, sell at the bid) and spot crypto (24/7). Cash account: no margin, no short selling, no naked option writing.
Process: Vamsi says where to look and how to trade. Each instruction is journaled with the trade it produced, and the stops and exits he sets are enforced at every routine run.

entries.title: Vamsi's strategy: buy support, sell resistance (25-name radar)
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Sat Oct 3): trade high-volatility stocks (his daily names: GPUS, IREN, BTDR); buy at support, sell at resistance, stop under support; keep at least 20 names on the radar with the levels ready; a name reaching its support is the trigger.
Radar: 25 names from Friday's closes (config/radar.json; table in research/radar/2026-10-03.md). Levels are swing lows and highs tested at least twice in the last 120 sessions. Buy zone = support to support + 0.3 ATR; stop = 0.6 ATR under support; sell zone = resistance - 0.3 ATR to resistance. GPUS (R:R 1.2, about $7M traded a day) and BTDR (R:R 1.4) miss the filters and stay on as his names.
Rules (RUNBOOK 2a): buy at a regular-session run from 9:55 AM when a name is inside its buy zone, or touched it this session and held with entry R:R of at least 1.5. Never after it trades through its stop, on an offering or negative-news day, or after 2:55 PM Monday. Up to 4 positions of about $250, at most 2 of them crypto-linked (13 of the 25 move with bitcoin or ether), higher R:R first, settled cash only on Monday. Sell in the sell zone, at the stop, or at the 3:40 PM liquidation Monday (unless the window is extended).
At Friday's close HUT ($89.70) and UMAC ($22.33) sit inside their buy zones; ASTS, ONDS, GLXY, NNE, TEM, SMCI, MSTR, GPUS and CORZ are within 3% above theirs.
This book trades only these instructions; stocks only under this strategy.

entries.title: Backtest: buying the radar's support has no measurable edge (61 stocks, 5 years)
entries.body:
Question from Vamsi: can I read levels, candles, trends and volume well enough? Test: scripts/sr_backtest.py rebuilds the radar's levels each day from the data available at that close (no look-ahead) for all 61 radar candidates over 5 years, then trades the next session. Costs are included, and a stop and target hit on the same day count as the stop.
Live rule (buy the touch of the buy zone; sell at the sell zone, the stop, or after 10 sessions): 2,560 trades, average +0.02R [-0.05, +0.10], +0.13% a trade, 34% winners, stop hit 63%. Random entries on the same stocks with the same stop and target distances: +0.01R. The level adds nothing measurable.
One-session version (sold at that day's close, the Monday-only case): 5,127 trades, -0.05R [-0.07, -0.03], -0.34% a trade.
Rejection candle at the zone, buy the next open: 994 trades, -0.02R; more winners (48%), smaller wins.
Filters (above the 200-day, rising 50-day, support tested 3+ times, quiet or heavy volume on the touch): no subset's interval excludes zero. Best hint: heavy volume on the touch (1.5x the 20-day average), +0.11R (n=387) and +0.20R with the candle (n=94), both inside noise.
By year (touch, 10 sessions): 2022 -0.28R, 2023 +0.17R, 2024 +0.25R, 2025 +0.03R, 2026 -0.10R. The result follows the market, not the levels.
Limits: one way of drawing levels (daily swing points); today's list of popular volatile stocks (survivorship); daily bars can't see intraday reclaims. Full output: research/backtests/sr-2026-10-03.md.

entries.title: Window extended 30 days: $2,000 target by the Wed Nov 4 close (Vamsi, Mon Oct 5)
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Mon Oct 5, about 3:15 PM ET): extend the trading window by 30 days; the target stays $2,000, now by the Wed Nov 4, 2026, 4:00 PM ET close. He also approved a morning clue scan.
What changes: no 3:40 PM liquidation today. POET, HUT, CIFR and UMAC stay open overnight under the radar rules: sold at the sell zone or when the stop trades. Buys use settled cash only, every day, so a stop can always be sold (a stock bought with unsettled proceeds can't be sold before T+1). The radar is rebuilt from each day's closes at the 4:20 PM review. Final day Wed Nov 4: no new buys after 2:55 PM, everything sold at the 3:40 PM run.
Morning clue scan (8:40 AM, from Tue Oct 6): radar and candidate names showing pre-move clues (a tested support right under the price, a tightening range, up-day volume outweighing down-day volume, higher lows, a tested resistance overhead, a pre-market move with the sector). Big intraday movers are logged with the clues they showed beforehand and why they were missed. A clue changes a trading rule only after it beats random entries in the 5-year backtest.
The math: $1,011 to $2,000 is +98% in 22 sessions, +3.2% a session compounded. The support rule's 5-year backtest edge is about zero (J0005), so at 4 positions of 25% the likely 30-day result sits near the starting value; reaching $2,000 at these rules takes an unusually good run. Bigger positions, options or more trades a day raise both the upside and the risk of a deep loss; each is a strategy change for Vamsi to make.

entries.title: Mover post-mortem Mon Oct 5: TEM +9%, UPST +7%, AFRM +6%, GRAB +4%
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Oct 5): when a watched name moves a lot, check whether it showed clues before the move and why the routines missed them, then watch for those clues. First post-mortem, from clues.py on the radar and its candidates (61 names, GRAB among them; Vamsi asked about GRAB).
- TEM +9.0% (1.3 ATR), on the radar: support 73.93 tested twice half an ATR below, higher lows, a 10% pullback inside an uptrend. Missed by the entry rule: the day's low (76.17) stayed 0.8% above the buy zone top (75.57).
- AFRM +5.6% (1.2 ATR), candidate: half an ATR above an 11-touch support at 69.18, higher lows. Missed by the R:R filter (1.36 < 1.5: resistance at 75.03 was only 6% above); it closed at 74.75, at that resistance. It joins the radar tonight on the new levels.
- UPST +6.8% (1.6 ATR), candidate: no clues (no tested support, heavier down-day volume); it moved with AFRM.
- GRAB +4.1% (1.0 ATR), candidate: four clues at Friday's close (on a support with lows of 3.07 twice, 5-day range 65% of normal, up-day volume 2.25x down-day, higher lows). Missed by a screen bug, fixed tonight: a tested zone within 0.1 ATR of the price was ignored. GRAB's daily range fell to 3.81% today, under the 4% filter, so it stays a candidate.
Base rate today: 2 of 13 names with 2+ clues (or a breakout watch) moved up 1+ ATR, 1 of 48 without. One session is an anecdote; the 5-year clue backtest decides which clues count.
Changes: clues.py scan at the 8:40 run (bounce setups, breakout watches, pre-market moves), clues.py movers in every market-hours run, this post-mortem after each close. levels.py now counts a tested zone at the price as support when two of its swings are lows (a zone at the price built from highs, like INTR and STNE after today's spikes, is old resistance).

entries.title: Clue backtest: none of the clues predicted next-day up-moves over 5 years
entries.body:
Test of the morning scan's clues (clues.py) before they are trusted: 66 candidates, 5 years of daily bars, 37,553 name-days on which the radar's volatility and liquidity filters passed (research/backtests/clues-2026-10-05.md; script scripts/clue_backtest.py, errors clustered by date).
Base rate: the next session closed 1+ ATR higher on 8.1% of name-days and 1+ ATR lower on 5.4%.
- Score 3+ (the scan alert): 7.9% up, 5.0% down. SUP + HL: 8.1% up, 4.5% down. Breakout watch (RES + COIL): 6.3% up. No lift.
- ACC (up-day volume 1.5x down-day): 10.6% up and 7.2% down: bigger moves both ways, not a direction.
- COIL (tight range): 5.8% up, 3.2% down: quiet days tend to stay quiet the next day.
- SUP (at tested support): 7.6% up, 4.0% down: fewer sharp drops, no extra upside.
- Buying the next open and selling that close lost 0.13-0.40% after costs in every group (score 4, 262 name-days: +0.34% +/- 0.67, not significant). Five-day returns were +1.3% for all name-days (these stocks rose over the period) and +1.8% for score 3+ or SUP + HL, inside the noise (+/- 0.7-0.8).
Conclusion: Monday's anecdote (2 of 13 clue names moved, 1 of 48 others) does not hold over 989 sessions. The morning scan stays a description of setups for Vamsi, not a forecast or a trade rule; the radar's entry rules are unchanged.

entries.title: Vamsi's direction (Oct 5): buy the day's deepest dips in the buy zone; read the news behind sudden moves; review every trade
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Mon Oct 5, evening), summarized: buying stocks that dipped hard in the opening hours, inside their buy zones near support with good R:R, and selling into the recovery is the skill to build; the opening fear often fades and many stocks settle less negative. When a stock moves suddenly, read the news behind it at once and judge how big it really is: stocks that fall too far on simple news recover. Review every bad trade, find the mistake and fix the strategy; consistent small gains matter more than one big day.
Applied from Tue Oct 6:
- Entry order: when more radar names are in BUY ZONE or BOUNCE than slots or settled cash allow, the deepest dip against the prior close (in ATR units) goes first, then the higher R:R. levels.py check now prints each name's move on the day and sorts the buy lists that way.
- News rule: only an offering or other dilution, or material company news (guidance cut, failed trial or rejection, regulatory or legal hit, delisting notice, accounting problem) cancels an entry. Sector-wide moves, analyst notes and recap headlines do not; a drop on minor news into the buy zone is a candidate.
- Trade reviews: every closed position gets a review entry (entry context, best and worst price held, exit, whether a rule should change); the first, provisional one is UMAC's.
Tested the same night (opening-dip backtest, next entry): the edge from buying the dip sits at the open, not at 9:55.

entries.title: Opening-dip backtest: gap-downs bought at the open recovered; dips bought at 9:55 or 10:30 did not
entries.body:
Test of Vamsi's dip-buying idea on the 66 radar candidates (scripts/dip_backtest.py; research/backtests/dip-2026-10-06.md). Entry against the prior close, exit at the prior close if the price gets back there that day, otherwise at the close; returns per trade after slippage, 95% intervals clustered by date; only days on which the radar's filters pass.
- At the open, 4 years (37,800 trades): a gap down of 0.5-0.75 ATR averaged +0.53% +/- 0.49 (57% winners); 0.75-1 ATR +0.83% +/- 1.03; 1+ ATR +1.13% +/- 1.94. All open entries averaged -0.32% +/- 0.16 and gap-ups -0.45%. Big gap-downs recover part of the drop during the day.
- At 10:30, 2 years (30,015): down 0.5-0.75 ATR -0.14% +/- 0.29; 0.75-1 ATR -0.13%; 1+ ATR +0.20% +/- 0.64. A stock still deep in the red after the first hour has no recovery edge.
- At 9:55, last 60 sessions (3,547): down 0.5-0.75 ATR -0.03% +/- 1.16; 1+ ATR +1.59% +/- 2.21 (78 trades). Inside the radar's buy zone, a 0.5+ ATR dip averaged +0.79% +/- 1.25 (90 trades) against -0.28% for smaller dips: the same direction in all three tests (open +0.41 vs -0.24; 10:30 -0.06 vs -0.42), none significant alone.
- Getting back to the prior close is rare after a deep dip: 4-21% of the time for dips of 0.5+ ATR.
Reading: the market does over-react at the open, but the recovery starts in the first minutes. Monday's three winners were 0.5 ATR dips bought at 9:55, the bucket that averages about zero: a good day, not yet a demonstrated edge. The dip-first ordering costs nothing and points the right way in every test, so it is now the entry order; an entry at the open needs a run near 9:31, which the schedule does not have.

entries.title: Trade review (open position): UMAC bought without a dip, faded 1.1% on day 1
entries.body:
UMAC 11.2455 sh bought at 9:56 AM Mon Oct 5 at 22.23 (quote 22.18): buy zone 21.82-22.34 (bought near the top), stop 20.79 (-6.5%), target 25.96 (+16.8%), entry R:R 2.6, fourth of four by R:R.

Path: up to 22.70 at 10:20 (+2.1%), then a slow fade all afternoon to 21.61 at 3:30 PM (-2.8%), close 21.99 (-1.1% from entry, -1.8% on the day) while the market rose.
Mistake? No rule was broken, and -1.1% is 0.14 ATR for a stock that moves 7.8% a day: noise so far. The trade is judged at its stop or target, the rule over many trades. The one difference from the winners: UMAC was bought without a dip. Under the dip-first order adopted tonight, LUNR (in its buy zone, -0.58 ATR at 9:55) would have taken this slot; LUNR rose 1.3% from 9:55 to the close while UMAC fell 1.6%. The same morning's counter-example: WULF, the deepest dip in the group (-0.64 ATR), ended 0.6% lower. Stays open: stop 20.79, target 25.96.

entries.title: Resting buy orders at support (Vamsi, Oct 5); stops become resting orders
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Mon Oct 5, night): set buys at the support price so they fill by themselves when the price touches it, so the book doesn't miss the big dips that happen between runs.
How it works from Tue Oct 6 (RUNBOOK 2c, scripts/orders.py), modeled on what a Robinhood cash account supports:
- At the 8:40 run, for each free slot with settled cash: a DAY buy limit at the buy-zone top of a radar name within 5% of its zone (R:R 1.5+, higher R:R first, at most 2 crypto-linked), about 25% of equity, reserved from settled cash. It fills when a 1-minute bar trades 1 cent through the limit, at the limit, or at the open when the stock gaps below it. Cancelled before the open if the pre-market price is at or under the stop, or when an offering or material company news appears.
- Every position's plan stop is now a resting stop order: it sells at the minute the stop trades (at the stop, or a lower open), instead of at the next run.
- Targets stay a run check, because a broker holds shares for one sell order at a time.
Test first (scripts/limit_backtest.py; research/backtests/limits-2026-10-06.md; 2 years of hourly bars, 5,832 days with a radar name within 5% of its zone): a limit at the zone top filled 63% of the time, a limit at support 42%, a run entry inside the zone 34%. Per trade, 3 sessions later: -0.04%, -0.12% and -0.25% (all +/- 0.5). Resting orders catch more dips and trade more often; they don't make each trade better. On Monday they would have bought POET, HUT, CIFR and UMAC at 9:30-9:36 on the first touch of the zone, 1-4% above the 9:56 prices actually paid.

entries.title: Resting buys move to support, the bottom of the buy zone; bitcoin gate for crypto-linked names (Vamsi, Oct 5)
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Mon Oct 5, night): put the resting buy at the bottom of the buy zone, so a deep dip in the first 30 minutes fills it automatically; prepare the buy levels for every radar name; buy only with confidence, good R:R and a good dip; and don't chase dips in crypto-linked stocks without checking bitcoin's sentiment.
Applied from Tue Oct 6: paper buy limits sit at support (the bottom of the zone), R:R measured from support (1.5+), names within 8% of support, higher R:R first. A bitcoin gate decides crypto-linked entries: open while bitcoin is above its 20-day average, down less than 2% on the day and less than 5% over 3 days (tonight: open, 85,302 against 82,858). The radar check already holds the buy level, stop and sell zone for every name; the broker-side limit order does the watching between runs.
Tested (research/backtests/limits-2026-10-06.md, 2 years of hourly bars): a limit at support fills 42% of the time against 63% at the zone top, and fills on deeper dips that often keep falling: the 0.6-ATR stop was hit within 3 sessions 62% of the time (49% from the zone top). Average result 3 sessions later: -0.12% from support, -0.04% from the zone top; with the stop 1.0 or 1.5 ATR under support, +0.08% and +0.21%, with 39% and 20% stopped out. All inside the noise: the bottom of the zone is a different trade-off (cheaper entries, fewer fills, more stop-outs), not a better trade.

entries.title: Replay practice: the rules over the last 30 sessions and 2.8 years, as if live (Vamsi, Oct 5)
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Mon Oct 5, night): practice the rules on the last 30 trading days as if live, without looking at what happened next, and learn from the bad cases.
Built scripts/replay.py. Each session uses only what was known then: the radar from the prior closes, the 8:40 resting limits, the bitcoin gate at 8:40, fills and stops bar by bar, targets and dip-first buys at the runs, T+1 settlement. No news filter. Reports in research/replay/.
Last 30 sessions (Aug 24-Oct 5, 5-minute bars), $1,000 under the Oct 6 rules: -6.4% (S&P 500 +1.2%, Nasdaq-100 +6.0%). 14 closed trades: 13 stopped, 1 target. 17 of 40 resting orders filled.
The bad cases:
- Support limits filled while the price fell through support: 9 of 14 never rose 0.5 ATR above the entry; 4 were stopped the session they were bought (RXRX and SMCI within 15 minutes of the Aug 24 open).
- 4 gapped through the stop overnight and sold at the open below it (-3.4% to -5.1%). RCAT, RGTI and SMR went together on Sep 10: three speculative small-caps, one bet.
- GPUS lost 9.1% and 10.2% (Sep 1 and 2) at full size: its stop sat about 9-10% under the entry, so a 25% position risked 2.3-2.5% of equity.
- GPUS, Aug 25: after a 6-session trading halt (Aug 17-24) the radar's "support" was the flat 0.45 halt print; the limit filled at the reopen and the stock fell 19% in 5 minutes.
- The one winner, RKLB (+21.6%), was bought at the open on a 0.83-ATR gap down and held 8 sessions to its target.
Over 2.8 years (hourly bars, 33 separate 22-session windows) the same rules made a median +4.8% (mean +1.9%), from -30% to +28%, and beat the S&P 500 in 17 of 33. None of the 25 variants tested doubled $1,000 in any 22-session window; the best 30-session window of any variant was +123%.
Trade by trade over 2.8 years (368 trades): +1.44% a trade (+/- 2.0), 19% winners averaging +32%, losers -5.8%. The rules make money only through rare targets. First-hour entries averaged +2.8% and entries after 10:30 -1.8% (+/- 2.2), yet stopping entries at 10:30 did not improve the windows; every other split (dip depth, gap, market direction, support strength, R:R) sat inside the noise.
Variants (research/replay/): limits at the zone top, run entries only, a 3-session time exit, stops 0.8-1.5 ATR, no bitcoin gate, R:R ranking, opening gap-down day trades, a 10:00 limit cancel, entry-time cutoffs, tested support for GPUS/IREN/BTDR, risk-based sizing. Results swing with the start date: the best of 15 variants on the last 60 sessions showed a +7.8% median and was ordinary over 2.8 years. Worse in every test: the 3-session exit. Worse in most: limits at the zone top. No bitcoin gate: worse over 2.8 years, better in the last 60 sessions.

entries.title: Rule changes from the replay: size from the stop; no orders in halted stocks
entries.body:
From Tue Oct 6 (RUNBOOK 2a, 2d), after the replay tests (J0018):
1. Size from the stop: each position is 25% of equity, cut so its stop loses at most 1.5% of equity (a stop 10% under the entry gets 15% of equity). levels.py check and orders.py plan print the size. In the replay it cut the worst 22-session window from -30% to -21% and raised the mean from +1.9% to +3.4% (median unchanged at +4.8%); the last 30 sessions went from -6.4% to +3.2%. It does not make trades better; it caps the GPUS-type loss.
2. No entry in a name with a zero-volume session in the last 5: levels.py check marks it HALTED and orders.py plan skips it.
Kept after testing: limits at support (the zone top was worse), the 0.6-ATR stop (wider stops gave no consistent gain), the bitcoin gate, dip-first ranking, holding to the target or the stop (a 3-session exit lost in every test), resting limits all day.
Rule for future changes: a new rule trades only after it beats the live rules on the mean and the worst window of the separate hourly windows without losing on the 5-minute windows. The Sunday review re-runs the 30-session replay and journals the week's bad cases.
On the target: no tested rule set doubled $1,000 in 22 sessions over 2.8 years. $2,000 by Nov 4 needs a run outside anything the replay produced.
Open positions (POET, HUT, CIFR, UMAC) keep the size, stop and target set at entry.

entries.title: PCVX: where the offering sell-off is most likely to reverse (Vamsi, Oct 6)
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Tue Oct 6, 9:45 AM): for PCVX, find the bottom where it will reverse.
Situation: Vaxcyte reported positive Phase 3 topline data for VAX-31 (OPUS-1, adults) on Mon Oct 5. The stock gapped from 56.48 to 87.21, hit 90.75 and closed 73.82 (+30.7%). That night it filed preliminary prospectuses for a stock offering (with pre-funded warrants) and concurrent convertible senior notes due 2032, amounts and price blank: not priced yet. Today 66.73 at 9:45 (-9.6%, low 65.70). Convertible buyers short the stock to hedge, and the stock offering usually prices at or below the pricing day's close.
Where a reversal is most likely (levels, not a forecast):
1. The stock offering's price, once announced (likely tonight). After pricing, a stock usually trades around the offering price for days, with the underwriters' stabilizing bid under it.
2. 58.27-59.64, the radar buy zone: the top of the three-week range before the data (support held 19 times), stop 55.52, sell zone 89.38-90.75 (Monday's high), R:R 7.2. It nearly fills Monday's gap (Friday's close 56.48).
3. Below that, support at 47.16.
Plan: no entry today or on the pricing day (offering, RUNBOOK 2a). From the session after, an entry if a slot is free and PCVX trades in 58.27-59.64 (BUY ZONE) or touches it and holds (BOUNCE). The post-close run reads the pricing and updates this plan.

entries.title: Focus: big dips with no fundamental reason, bought where they reverse (Vamsi, Oct 6)
entries.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Tue Oct 6, 10:00 AM): the paper book's gain came from dip recoveries, so focus on big dips. For each one, first find why it fell: company news that changes the business (offering, guidance cut, failed trial, legal or regulatory hit) or market and sector emotion with no company reason. Skip the first kind; for the second, find the support where it is likely to reverse and buy the reversal.
Check against the book so far: POET, HUT and CIFR, bought at 9:56 Mon Oct 5 while 2.9-4.1% (about 0.5 ATR) under their prior closes with no company news, made $45.35 of the $49.32 gain by 9:55 Tue; UMAC, bought without a dip, made $3.98. Four trades in a rising market (SPY +1.3% since the book started): consistent with the idea, not proof.
How it maps onto the rules: entries already go deepest dip first at support (2a, Oct 5), and company news that changes the business already cancels an entry. What is new is making the dip's cause the first question and waiting for the reversal. Test first (RUNBOOK 2d): scripts/news_dip_backtest.py compares dips with and without company news (SEC filings), at support or not, market-wide or not, buying the dip's close, the next open, or after a confirming up close. Results and any rule change follow in a research entry.
